title: Unload a part from a cycling shuttle table during its pause
instruction: Take the orange block off the moving shuttle and put it in the blue tray. The shuttle keeps cycling and won't stop for you.
context: Shuttle tables and indexing transfer lines bring parts to a station on a fixed cycle and pause only briefly; whoever unloads them must grab each part during the pause and be clear before the machine moves on. Done by: machine tenders and assembly-line workers.
setup: The two arm bases stand 61 cm apart on an oak table. Two steel rails (1.5 x 1.5 cm, 46 cm long) run across the table, parallel to the line through the arm bases, 30 and 38 cm in front of it, centred 3 cm toward the left arm from the midpoint between the bases. A grey steel shuttle plate (12 x 12 x 2 cm) rides on them, centred 34 cm in front of the bases; its two stops are 12 cm toward the right arm and 18 cm toward the left arm from the midpoint between the bases. It starts at its right stop. A bare aluminium block (5 x 5 x 3 cm, 200 g) lies flat in the middle of the shuttle, square to it. A blue plastic open tray (14 x 14 cm outside, 12 x 12 cm inside, 1 cm floor, 4 cm walls) stands on the table, square to the rails, its centre 17 cm in front of the bases and 5.5 cm outside the left arm's base. The shuttle's cycle, from the start: it waits 2.5 s at its right stop, travels 30 cm to its left stop in 2.5 s (smooth start and stop, peak speed 19 cm/s), waits 2.5 s, travels back in 2.5 s, and repeats every 10 s.
scoring: 1.0 if the block ends lying in the tray: its centre inside the tray's walls, its underside within 1 cm of the tray floor, still for 1 s. Otherwise the best reached during the trial: 0.5 if the block's centre was at some point inside the tray's walls with its underside less than 5 cm above the tray's rim; 0.25 if its underside was at some point 3 cm or more above the shuttle's top surface; otherwise 0 (the block never lifted, pushed off the shuttle, or knocked to the table).
reset_notes: Stop the shuttle at its right stop, put the block back in its middle, and start the cycle with the trial (beginning with the 2.5 s wait).
fidelity: The shuttle follows its path exactly, like a stiff servo axis: the arms can't push it or stop it, where a real drive would fault if blocked. It rides 2 mm above its rails. The block has the station's rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), more than aluminium on steel; at a peak acceleration under 0.5 m/s², it doesn't slide on the shuttle either way.
